description: A password is asked for by NAME in every library that takes one, so the rule reads the option rather than an argument position -- and it is scoped to the calls that OPEN A CONNECTION. Matching any call with a password option was tried and produced 265 findings across the clean corpus, almost all of them test helpers and assertions. The negative connection reads its password from the environment, which is not a literal; an option whose key is known while its value is not written down is treated as absent, which is what stops `{ password: req.body.password }` reading as a hard-coded one. The decode route is a negative that used to be a positive: reading a token without verifying it is ordinary, and the defect is trusting the claims afterwards.

expected.note: a password written into a connection config
